music-decades.title: Music of the Decades (1930s-2020s)
music-decades.description: From big band swing, rock & roll and Motown to 80s synth-pop, 90s grunge and modern pop anthems.

questions.prompt: Which bandleader made 'Sing, Sing, Sing (With a Swing)' famous at Carnegie Hall in 1938?
questions.explanation: Benny Goodman's historic 1938 Carnegie Hall jazz concert cemented swing music as a respected art form.

questions.prompt: Who wrote the iconic 1930 jazz standard 'Mood Indigo'?
questions.explanation: Duke Ellington recorded 'Mood Indigo' in 1930, featuring muted trumpet and trombone.

questions.prompt: Which legendary Delta blues guitarist was famed for recording 'Cross Road Blues' in 1936?
questions.explanation: Robert Johnson recorded 'Cross Road Blues' in San Antonio, Texas, in November 1936.

questions.prompt: Judy Garland immortalized 'Over the Rainbow' in which 1939 classic musical film?
questions.explanation: 'Over the Rainbow' won the Academy Award for Best Original Song for The Wizard of Oz in 1939.

questions.prompt: Which jazz vocalist made 'Strange Fruit' a historic protest anthem in 1939?
questions.explanation: Billie Holiday premiered Abel Meeropol's anti-lynching poem 'Strange Fruit' at Café Society in 1939.

questions.prompt: Which swing trombonist and bandleader formed his famous orchestra in 1937 and recorded 'Moonlight Serenade' in 1939?
questions.explanation: Glenn Miller's 'Moonlight Serenade' became his signature theme song.

questions.prompt: Ella Fitzgerald scored her first major number one hit in 1938 with which nursery rhyme adaptation?
questions.explanation: Recorded with the Chick Webb Orchestra, 'A-Tisket, A-Tasket' brought 21-year-old Ella international fame.

questions.prompt: Which French-Romani guitarist formed the Quintette du Hot Club de France in 1934 with Stéphane Grappelli?
questions.explanation: Django Reinhardt pioneered gypsy jazz guitar despite having two paralyzed fingers on his left hand.

questions.prompt: Cab Calloway popularized the phrase 'Hi-De-Ho' in which 1931 million-selling jazz track?
questions.explanation: 'Minnie the Moocher' made Cab Calloway the first African American musician to sell a million records.

questions.prompt: George Gershwin composed which groundbreaking 1935 American folk opera featuring 'Summertime'?
questions.explanation: 'Summertime' is one of the most covered songs in music history, originally written for Porgy and Bess.

questions.prompt: Who was known as the 'Singing Brakeman' and father of country music before his death in 1933?
questions.explanation: Jimmie Rodgers recorded famous blue yodels and is recognized as the father of country music.

questions.prompt: Which singing cowboy popularized 'Back in the Saddle Again' starting in 1939?
questions.explanation: Gene Autry co-wrote and recorded 'Back in the Saddle Again', becoming his signature tune.

questions.prompt: Which blues pianist and singer popularized boogie-woogie with 'Roll 'Em Pete' in 1938 with Big Joe Turner?
questions.explanation: Pete Johnson and Big Joe Turner helped spark the boogie-woogie craze at Carnegie Hall's 'From Spirituals to Swing'.

questions.prompt: Who recorded 'Cross Road Blues' and 'Sweet Home Chicago' during his brief 1936-1937 sessions?
questions.explanation: Robert Johnson recorded 29 legendary songs across two sessions in Texas.

questions.prompt: Which bandleader's signature tune was 'One O'Clock Jump', first recorded in 1937?
questions.explanation: 'One O'Clock Jump' became Count Basie's theme song and a swing era standard.

questions.prompt: Who sang 'Night and Day' when it debuted in Cole Porter's 1932 musical 'Gay Divorce'?
questions.explanation: Fred Astaire introduced 'Night and Day' on Broadway before starring in the 1934 film adaptation.

questions.prompt: Which clarinetist rivaled Benny Goodman with hits like 'Begin the Beguine' in 1938?
questions.explanation: Artie Shaw's arrangement of Cole Porter's 'Begin the Beguine' sold millions of copies.

questions.prompt: In 1935, which electronic instrument was introduced by Laurens Hammond, revolutionizing gospel and jazz?
questions.explanation: The Hammond organ was patented in 1934 and manufactured beginning in 1935.

questions.prompt: Which folk singer and activist wrote 'This Land Is Your Land' in 1940 based on tunes heard during the 1930s Dust Bowl?
questions.explanation: Woody Guthrie wrote 'This Land Is Your Land' as a critical response to Irving Berlin's 'God Bless America'.

questions.prompt: Which trumpeter was nicknamed 'Satchmo' and recorded 'West End Blues' and 'When the Saints Go Marching In' in the 1930s?
questions.explanation: Louis Armstrong's 1938 recording of 'When the Saints Go Marching In' popularized the New Orleans spiritual.

questions.prompt: Which pianist recorded 'Honky Tonk Train Blues' in the 1930s, defining boogie-woogie piano?
questions.explanation: Meade Lux Lewis first recorded 'Honky Tonk Train Blues' in 1927 and re-recorded it in 1935 to huge acclaim.

questions.prompt: Who wrote and recorded the 1934 jazz stride masterpiece 'Ain't Misbehavin'' and 'Honeysuckle Rose'?
questions.explanation: Fats Waller was a comedic genius and one of the most prolific stride pianists of the 1930s.

questions.prompt: Which Bing Crosby recording from 1942 holds the Guinness World Record for best-selling physical single of all time?
questions.explanation: Irving Berlin's 'White Christmas' sung by Bing Crosby has sold over 50 million physical copies worldwide.

questions.prompt: Which bebop trumpet pioneer co-created modern jazz alongside Charlie Parker in the mid-1940s?
questions.explanation: Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie 'Bird' Parker developed the rapid chord progressions and angular solos of bebop in the 1940s.

questions.prompt: Which alto saxophonist, nicknamed 'Bird', was the supreme improviser of 1940s bebop?
questions.explanation: Charlie Parker transformed modern jazz harmony with recordings at Minton's Playhouse and Savoy Records.

questions.prompt: Frank Sinatra caused riots among teenage bobby-soxers at which legendary New York venue in October 1944?
questions.explanation: The Columbus Day riot of 1944 at the Paramount Theatre saw over 30,000 screaming teenage fans jam Times Square.

questions.prompt: The Andrews Sisters had a massive 1941 wartime boogie-woogie hit with which song?

options.B: Don't Sit Under the Apple Tree

questions.explanation: 'Boogie Woogie Bugle Boy' was recorded in 1941 for Abbott and Costello's film 'Buck Privates'.

questions.prompt: Glenn Miller was awarded the first official gold record in 1942 for selling 1.2 million copies of which song?
questions.explanation: RCA Victor surprised Glenn Miller on a radio broadcast with a gold-lacquered master of 'Chattanooga Choo Choo'.

questions.prompt: Which French singer recorded 'La Vie en rose' in 1946, becoming her signature international song?
questions.explanation: 'The Little Sparrow' Édith Piaf wrote the lyrics to 'La Vie en rose' in 1945, releasing it in 1947.

questions.prompt: Which jazz pianist and vocalist recorded 'Straighten Up and Fly Right' with his trio in 1943?
questions.explanation: Nat King Cole's trio hit launched Capitol Records into a major recording powerhouse.

questions.prompt: Who recorded 'Caldonia' in 1945, leading the jump blues revolution with his Tympany Five?
questions.explanation: Louis Jordan is hailed as 'The King of the Jukebox' and an essential bridge to rock and roll.

questions.prompt: Which country icon wrote and recorded 'Move It On Over' in 1947 and 'I'm So Lonesome I Could Cry' in 1949?
questions.explanation: Hank Williams became country music's most celebrated songwriter through his 1940s recordings on MGM.

questions.prompt: In 1948, Columbia Records unveiled which revolutionary vinyl format spinning at 33 1/3 RPM?
questions.explanation: Columbia engineer Peter Goldmark led the team that introduced the 12-inch 33 1/3 RPM LP in June 1948.

questions.prompt: RCA Victor responded in 1949 with which format designed specifically for singles?
questions.explanation: RCA Victor introduced the durable 45 RPM 7-inch vinyl with a large center hole in early 1949.

questions.prompt: Which pianist composed the bebop masterpiece ''Round Midnight', first recorded by Cootie Williams in 1944?
questions.explanation: Thelonious Monk's ''Round Midnight' is the most recorded jazz standard written by any jazz musician.

questions.prompt: Which blues legend recorded 'Boogie Chillen'' in Detroit in 1948, hitting number one on the R&B chart?
questions.explanation: John Lee Hooker's driving foot-stomping electric guitar on 'Boogie Chillen'' popularized electric blues.

questions.prompt: Muddy Waters moved from Mississippi to Chicago in 1943 and recorded which breakthrough 1948 hit on Aristocrat Records?
questions.explanation: 'I Can't Be Satisfied' featured Muddy's electrified bottleneck slide and sold out its first run in Chicago within a day.

questions.prompt: Which crooner scored a 1945 million-seller with 'Till the End of Time', based on Chopin's Polonaise?
questions.explanation: Perry Como had one of the longest consecutive charting careers in mid-century vocal pop.

questions.prompt: Woody Herman's big band was famously nicknamed what during the 1940s?
questions.explanation: Woody Herman's 'First Herd' in 1944-1946 blended roaring swing with modern bebop influences.

questions.prompt: Which calypso-inspired hit song by The Andrews Sisters in 1945 sparked a copyright controversy regarding Lord Invader?
questions.explanation: The Andrews Sisters scored a multi-million seller with Morey Amsterdam's unauthorized adaptation of Lord Invader's calypso.

questions.prompt: Who recorded 'Lover Man (Oh, Where Can You Be?)' with strings in 1944, her first pop chart crossover?
questions.explanation: Billie Holiday specifically requested a string section for 'Lover Man' on Decca Records.

questions.prompt: Peggy Lee gained widespread fame singing 'Why Don't You Do Right?' in 1942 with which bandleader?
questions.explanation: Peggy Lee's sultry vocal on 'Why Don't You Do Right?' sold over a million copies and made her a star.

questions.prompt: Which blues shouter recorded 'Good Rocking Tonight' in 1947, later covered by Wynonie Harris and Elvis Presley?
questions.explanation: Roy Brown's 1947 recording of 'Good Rocking Tonight' is widely considered a foundational rock precursor.

questions.prompt: Which electric guitar pioneer recorded 'Call It Stormy Monday Blues' in 1947?
questions.explanation: T-Bone Walker was among the first to explore the solo melodic capabilities of the electric guitar.

questions.prompt: Which 1954 Bill Haley & His Comets single became an anthem for the youth revolution after featuring in 'Blackboard Jungle'?
questions.explanation: 'Rock Around the Clock' hit #1 on the Billboard pop chart in July 1955, igniting global rock and roll.

questions.prompt: Sam Phillips founded which Memphis recording studio that discovered Elvis Presley, Johnny Cash, and Jerry Lee Lewis?
questions.explanation: Sun Records at 706 Union Avenue in Memphis launched rockabilly and rock and roll into American culture.

questions.prompt: Chuck Berry's first major hit for Chess Records in 1955, adapted from the country tune 'Ida Red', was what?
questions.explanation: 'Maybellene' sold over a million copies and established Chuck Berry's signature double-stop guitar intro.

questions.prompt: Which flamboyant Macon, Georgia pianist roared into the charts in late 1955 with 'Tutti Frutti'?
questions.explanation: Little Richard's vocal 'A-wop-bop-a-loo-bop-a-lop-bam-boom!' became a founding clarion call of rock and roll.

questions.prompt: Which New Orleans pianist and singer crossed over to pop stardom with 'Ain't That a Shame' in 1955 and 'Blueberry Hill' in 1956?
questions.explanation: Fats Domino sold over 65 million records, second in 1950s rock sales only to Elvis Presley.

questions.prompt: Elvis Presley made his television debut on national TV performing 'Heartbreak Hotel' in 1956 on which variety show?
questions.explanation: Elvis first appeared on the Dorsey Brothers' Stage Show in January 1956 before his famous Ed Sullivan appearances.

questions.prompt: Which 1959 Miles Davis album remains the best-selling modal jazz album in history?
questions.explanation: Recorded over two days with John Coltrane and Bill Evans, 'Kind of Blue' is universally recognized as a jazz masterpiece.

questions.prompt: Buddy Holly and The Crickets topped the UK and US charts in 1957 with which song inspired by a John Wayne quote?
questions.explanation: John Wayne's repeated line 'That'll be the day' in the 1956 western 'The Searchers' inspired Holly's hit.

questions.prompt: February 3, 1959 became known as 'The Day the Music Died' following a plane crash that claimed Buddy Holly, Ritchie Valens, and whom?
questions.explanation: The chartered Beechcraft Bonanza crashed near Clear Lake, Iowa, during the Winter Dance Party tour.

questions.prompt: Johnny Cash achieved immortality with which 1956 Sun Records hit pledging marital devotion?
questions.explanation: 'I Walk the Line' was Johnny Cash's first Billboard country number one and crossed over into the top 20 pop chart.

questions.prompt: Ray Charles combined gospel sanctified singing with R&B in which 1959 smash hit featuring call-and-response?
questions.explanation: 'What'd I Say' was improvised live during a dance in late 1958 when Charles had extra set time to fill.

questions.prompt: Who recorded 'Jailhouse Rock' and 'Hound Dog' during his peak 1956-1957 rock and roll reign?
questions.explanation: Jerry Leiber and Mike Stoller wrote 'Jailhouse Rock' for Elvis's 1957 musical film.

questions.prompt: Jerry Lee Lewis shocked fans and ruined his 1958 UK tour when the press revealed he had married whom?
questions.explanation: The revelation devastated Jerry Lee Lewis's mainstream pop career for a decade.

questions.prompt: Which 1958 instrumental rock track by Link Wray is credited with pioneering the power chord and distortion fuzz?
questions.explanation: 'Rumble' was actually banned by several radio stations for fear its aggressive sound would incite teenage gang fights.

questions.prompt: Dave Brubeck Quartet released which groundbreaking 1959 5/4 time signature jazz composition composed by Paul Desmond?
questions.explanation: 'Take Five' became the biggest-selling jazz single of all time from the album 'Time Out'.

questions.prompt: Who recorded 'Blue Suede Shoes' first at Sun Records in December 1955 before Elvis Presley covered it?
questions.explanation: Carl Perkins wrote 'Blue Suede Shoes' on a brown paper potato sack after seeing a dancer at a gig.

questions.prompt: Which female rockabilly pioneer recorded 'Let's Have a Party' and 'Fujiyama Mama' in the late 1950s?
questions.explanation: Wanda Jackson was encouraged by Elvis Presley to pivot from pure country to fiery rock and roll.

questions.prompt: The Coasters had smash comedic rock and roll hits written by Leiber & Stoller including 'Yakety Yak' and which 1959 track?
questions.explanation: 'Charlie Brown' featured King Curtis's famous tenor saxophone breaks and comedic vocal hooks.

questions.prompt: Which 1958 novelty hit by The Champs consisted of an infectious Latin mambo groove and one spoken word?
questions.explanation: 'Tequila' reached number one on the Billboard pop charts and won the Grammy for Best R&B Performance.

questions.prompt: Which 17-year-old Chicano rock pioneer recorded 'La Bamba' and 'Donna' in 1958 before his tragic death in 1959?
questions.explanation: Ritchie Valens adapted the traditional Mexican folk song 'La Bamba' into an energetic three-chord rock anthem.

questions.prompt: Which doo-wop group topped the charts in 1956 with 'The Great Pretender' and 'My Prayer'?
questions.explanation: The Platters, led by lead tenor Tony Williams, were one of the most successful vocal groups of the 1950s.

questions.prompt: Who wrote and recorded the 1957 rock anthem 'Peggy Sue', named after the Crickets drummer's girlfriend?
questions.explanation: The song was originally titled 'Cindy Lou' before drummer Jerry Allison asked Holly to rename it after his girlfriend.

questions.prompt: The Beatles made their record-breaking first US appearance on The Ed Sullivan Show in February of which year?
questions.explanation: On February 9, 1964, over 73 million viewers tuned in to watch The Beatles on Ed Sullivan, launching the British Invasion.

questions.prompt: Which 1967 Beatles album is widely considered a defining masterwork of the psychedelic era?

options.C: Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band

questions.explanation: Sgt. Pepper spent 27 weeks at number one on the UK album chart and won four Grammy Awards in 1968.

questions.prompt: Berry Gordy Jr. founded Motown Records in Detroit, famously branding the label's signature sound as what?
questions.explanation: Motown's Hitsville U.S.A. studio churned out hundreds of crossover soul hits under Gordy's quality control system.

questions.prompt: Which Motown female vocal trio achieved 12 Billboard Hot 100 number-one singles between 1964 and 1969?
questions.explanation: Led by Diana Ross, The Supremes became Motown's most commercially successful act.

questions.prompt: Which 1965 Bob Dylan single electrified folk rock with the opening snare crack and sneering refrain?
questions.explanation: 'Like a Rolling Stone' smashed the unwritten rule that pop singles had to be under three minutes by running over six minutes.

questions.prompt: Jimi Hendrix famously set his Fender Stratocaster on fire at which 1967 American music festival?
questions.explanation: Hendrix's incendiary performance of 'Wild Thing' at Monterey in June 1967 launched him into superstar status.

questions.prompt: Which legendary 1969 festival in Bethel, New York, drew over 400,000 attendees under the banner '3 Days of Peace & Music'?
questions.explanation: Woodstock took place from August 15-18, 1969, featuring iconic sets by Hendrix, Santana, The Who, and Crosby, Stills & Nash.

questions.prompt: Brian Wilson spent over six months crafting which ambitious 1966 Beach Boys single known as a 'pocket symphony'?
questions.explanation: 'Good Vibrations' cost an unprecedented $50,000 to produce in 1966 across four different Los Angeles recording studios.

questions.prompt: Aretha Franklin demanded 'R-E-S-P-E-C-T' in her 1967 Atlantic Records smash, originally written and recorded by whom?
questions.explanation: Otis Redding wrote and released 'Respect' in 1965, but Aretha transformed it into a feminist and civil rights anthem.

questions.prompt: Which British rock band released 'My Generation' in 1965 featuring Pete Townshend's stuttering vocals and guitar smashing?
questions.explanation: 'My Generation' became an anthem for teenage frustration and featured John Entwistle's famous bass solos.

questions.prompt: The Rolling Stones scored their first US number one hit in 1965 with which fuzz-guitar riff anthem?
questions.explanation: Keith Richards woke up in a hotel room in Clearwater, Florida, with the guitar riff in his head and recorded it on a cassette.

questions.prompt: Which lead singer of The Doors was known as 'The Lizard King' before his death in Paris in 1971?
questions.explanation: Jim Morrison's poetic lyrics and provocative stage persona propelled The Doors on hits like 'Light My Fire'.

questions.prompt: Simon & Garfunkel's career was saved in 1965 when producer Tom Wilson overdubbed electric instruments onto which acoustic track?
questions.explanation: The overdubbed electric version soared to number one on the Billboard Hot 100 on New Year's Day 1966.

questions.prompt: Which legendary studio house band played on almost every classic 1960s Motown hit in Detroit?
questions.explanation: The Funk Brothers played on more number one records than The Beatles, Elvis, The Beach Boys, and The Stones combined.

questions.prompt: Which Los Angeles session collective played on hits for The Beach Boys, The Monkees, The Mamas & the Papas, and Frank Sinatra?
questions.explanation: Bassist Carol Kaye, drummer Hal Blaine, and guitarist Glen Campbell were key members of the Wrecking Crew.

questions.prompt: Janis Joplin rose to international stardom as the explosive blues-rock lead singer of which San Francisco band?

options.B: Big Brother and the Holding Company

questions.explanation: Big Brother's 1968 album 'Cheap Thrills' featured Joplin's devastating vocal on 'Piece of My Heart'.

questions.prompt: The Velvet Underground released their seminal banana-covered debut album in 1967 in collaboration with which German singer?
questions.explanation: Andy Warhol produced the album and paired the band with German model and singer Nico.

questions.prompt: Which Kinks single from 1964 pioneered heavy metal power riffs through a slashed speaker cone amplifier?

options.B: All Day and All of the Night

questions.explanation: Dave Davies sliced his amplifier's speaker cone with a razor blade to achieve the raw, distorted guitar tone.

questions.prompt: Otis Redding recorded '(Sittin' On) The Dock of the Bay' just three days before what tragic event in December 1967?

options.A: He died in a plane crash in Wisconsin
options.C: He was drafted into the military

questions.explanation: The song was released posthumously and became the first posthumous number-one single in US chart history.

questions.prompt: Which instrumental surf rock track by The Surfaris in 1963 was famous for its opening cackle and blistering drum solo?
questions.explanation: Ron Wilson's drum solos on 'Wipe Out' inspired a whole generation of rock drummers.

questions.prompt: Which 1969 Creedence Clearwater Revival song became an anthem of opposition to the Vietnam War draft?

options.C: Have You Ever Seen the Rain

questions.explanation: John Fogerty wrote 'Fortunate Son' criticizing how the wealthy elite could avoid the military draft.

questions.prompt: Which legendary singer released 'A Change Is Gonna Come' in 1964, becoming an iconic civil rights movement anthem?
questions.explanation: Inspired by Bob Dylan's 'Blowin' in the Wind' and Cooke's own experiences with racism, the song was released posthumously.

questions.prompt: Which Swedish pop group won the Eurovision Song Contest in Brighton in 1974 with 'Waterloo'?
questions.explanation: ABBA's Brighton Eurovision victory launched Agnetha, Björn, Benny, and Anni-Frid into global superstardom.

questions.prompt: Queen's operatic rock masterpiece 'Bohemian Rhapsody' was released in 1975 on which studio album?
questions.explanation: Freddie Mercury layered over 180 vocal overdubs to create the operatic mid-section of 'Bohemian Rhapsody'.

questions.prompt: Led Zeppelin's 1971 untitled fourth album (Led Zeppelin IV) featured which iconic epic acoustic-to-hard-rock track?
questions.explanation: Jimmy Page and Robert Plant composed 'Stairway to Heaven' at the Bron-Yr-Aur cottage in Wales.

questions.prompt: Pink Floyd's 1973 concept album 'The Dark Side of the Moon' spent how many cumulative weeks on the Billboard charts?
questions.explanation: Dark Side of the Moon remained on the Billboard 200 for an astonishing 900+ weeks from 1973 through the 1980s.

questions.prompt: Which British glam rock icon introduced his alien rockstar alter ego Ziggy Stardust in 1972?
questions.explanation: 'The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars' established David Bowie as a chameleon of rock theatre.

questions.prompt: Which Donna Summer and Giorgio Moroder track from 1977 revolutionized electronic dance music with modular synthesizers?
questions.explanation: Brian Eno famously told David Bowie that 'I Feel Love' was the sound of the future and would change club music for 15 years.

questions.prompt: Fleetwood Mac recorded their 1977 multi-platinum album 'Rumours' amidst what personal turmoil?

options.A: All band members were breaking up with each other
options.B: The departure of their lead guitarist
options.D: A fierce legal lawsuit with their label

questions.explanation: The Lindsey Buckingham/Stevie Nicks and John/Christine McVie divorces fueled the emotional songwriting on 'Rumours'.

questions.prompt: Which 1977 soundtrack album by the Bee Gees became one of the biggest-selling albums in history and ignited the disco inferno?
questions.explanation: Saturday Night Fever featured hits like 'Stayin' Alive', 'Night Fever', and 'How Deep Is Your Love'.

questions.prompt: Which British punk rock quartet shocked the UK in 1977 with the jubilee protest single 'God Save the Queen'?
questions.explanation: The BBC banned 'God Save the Queen', yet it officially reached number two on the UK Singles Chart.

questions.prompt: The Clash released their definitive double-album 'London Calling' in December of which year?
questions.explanation: London Calling blended punk with reggae, ska, rockabilly, and soul, and is considered one of rock's finest albums.

questions.prompt: Bob Marley and the Wailers released which 1977 masterpiece album recorded in London featuring 'One Love' and 'Jamming'?
questions.explanation: Time magazine named Bob Marley's 'Exodus' the best album of the 20th century in 1999.

questions.prompt: Stevie Wonder achieved a historic 'classic period' winning three Album of the Year Grammys for 'Innervisions', 'Fulfillingness' First Finale', and which 1976 double album?

options.D: Songs in the Key of Life

questions.explanation: 'Songs in the Key of Life' debuted at number one on the Billboard 200 and produced hits like 'Sir Duke' and 'Isn't She Lovely'.

questions.prompt: Which American rock band released 'Hotel California' in late 1976, featuring Don Felder and Joe Walsh's dueling guitar solos?
questions.explanation: 'Hotel California' won the 1977 Grammy Award for Record of the Year and has sold over 32 million copies.

questions.prompt: Which 1979 single by The Sugarhill Gang is recognized as the first commercially successful hip-hop record?
questions.explanation: 'Rapper's Delight' sampled the rhythm track of Chic's 'Good Times' and reached the top 40 of the Billboard Hot 100.

questions.prompt: Which Southern rock band wrote 'Sweet Home Alabama' in 1974 as a rebuttal to Neil Young's songs 'Southern Man' and 'Alabama'?
questions.explanation: Ed King, Gary Rossington, and Ronnie Van Zant co-wrote 'Sweet Home Alabama'.

questions.prompt: Blondie crossed over from New York CBGB punk to disco pop in 1979 with which international chart-topper?
questions.explanation: Debbie Harry and Chris Stein wrote 'Heart of Glass' using a Roland drum machine and disco four-on-the-floor beat.

questions.prompt: Which German electronic music group released 'Autobahn' in 1974 and 'Trans-Europe Express' in 1977, laying the blueprint for techno?
questions.explanation: Ralf Hütter and Florian Schneider created minimalist electronic pop utilizing custom electronic vocoders and drum pads.

questions.prompt: Which funk pioneer led the Parliament-Funkadelic collective, landing the 'Mothership' on stage in 1976?
questions.explanation: George Clinton created P-Funk mythology with albums like 'Mothership Connection' and 'One Nation Under a Groove'.

questions.prompt: AC/DC released which breakthrough 1979 hard rock album, the last to feature lead singer Bon Scott before his death?
questions.explanation: Produced by Mutt Lange, 'Highway to Hell' catapulted the Australian hard rock band into international arenas.

questions.prompt: Meat Loaf and composer Jim Steinman released which operatic rock phenomenon in 1977, featuring 'Paradise by the Dashboard Light'?
questions.explanation: 'Bat Out of Hell' spent over 500 weeks on the UK album charts and has sold over 43 million copies.

questions.prompt: Kate Bush made chart history in 1978 with which debut single, becoming the first female artist to achieve a UK #1 with a self-written song?

options.A: The Man with the Child in His Eyes

questions.explanation: At age 19, Kate Bush topped the UK singles chart for four weeks with her literary Emily Brontë homage.

questions.prompt: Which Australian soft-rock duo had massive late-1970s and early-1980s love ballad hits like 'Lost in Love' and 'All Out of Love'?
questions.explanation: Graham Russell and Russell Hitchcock formed Air Supply in Melbourne after meeting on the production of Jesus Christ Superstar.

questions.prompt: Michael Jackson's 1982 album 'Thriller' was produced by which legendary maestro?
questions.explanation: Quincy Jones produced 'Off the Wall', 'Thriller', and 'Bad', with 'Thriller' becoming the best-selling album of all time.

questions.prompt: On May 16, 1983, Michael Jackson first unveiled which signature dance move during 'Billie Jean' on the Motown 25 TV special?
questions.explanation: Jackson's moonwalk performance mesmerized over 47 million television viewers and sparked a worldwide dance craze.

questions.prompt: MTV officially launched in the United States on August 1, 1981, with which music video as its maiden broadcast?

options.D: 'Video Killed the Radio Star' by The Buggles

questions.explanation: The Buggles' ironic synth-pop video opened the MTV broadcast at 12:01 AM on August 1, 1981.

questions.prompt: Prince wrote, arranged, composed, and performed which 1984 rock musical soundtrack and blockbuster film?
questions.explanation: 'Purple Rain' won the Academy Award for Best Original Song Score and spent 24 consecutive weeks at #1 on the Billboard 200.

questions.prompt: Which July 13, 1985 dual-venue benefit concert organized by Bob Geldof and Midge Ure raised funds for Ethiopian famine relief?
questions.explanation: Held simultaneously at Wembley Stadium in London and JFK Stadium in Philadelphia, Live Aid reached an estimated 1.9 billion viewers.

questions.prompt: Which band's 21-minute set at Wembley Stadium during Live Aid in 1985 is widely cited as the greatest rock performance in history?
questions.explanation: Freddie Mercury commanded 72,000 spectators with 'Bohemian Rhapsody', 'Radio Ga Ga', and 'We Will Rock You'.

questions.prompt: Madonna released which 1984 sophomore album featuring 'Material Girl' and the Nile Rodgers-produced title track?
questions.explanation: 'Like a Virgin' was Madonna's first Billboard 200 #1 album and sold over 21 million copies worldwide.

questions.prompt: Whitney Houston scored seven consecutive Billboard Hot 100 #1 singles in the 1980s, beginning with which 1985 ballad?

options.A: Saving All My Love for You

questions.explanation: Whitney Houston surpassed both The Beatles and The Bee Gees by charting seven straight #1 singles.

questions.prompt: Guns N' Roses released which 1987 debut studio album that remains the best-selling debut album of all time in the US?
questions.explanation: 'Appetite for Destruction' sold over 30 million copies worldwide and featured 'Sweet Child o' Mine' and 'Welcome to the Jungle'.

questions.prompt: U2 achieved massive global success with which 1987 album featuring 'With or Without You' and 'Where the Streets Have No Name'?
questions.explanation: Produced by Brian Eno and Daniel Lanois, 'The Joshua Tree' won the Grammy for Album of the Year in 1988.

questions.prompt: Which British synth-pop duo topped charts in 1986 with 'West End Girls'?
questions.explanation: Neil Tennant and Chris Lowe's hip-hop-influenced synth track 'West End Girls' topped both the US and UK charts.

questions.prompt: Run-DMC collaborated with Steven Tyler and Joe Perry in 1986 to record a historic rap-rock crossover cover of which song?
questions.explanation: The 1986 remake of 'Walk This Way' broke hip-hop into mainstream MTV rotation and revived Aerosmith's career.

questions.prompt: Which 1983 New Order single became the best-selling 12-inch vinyl single of all time?
questions.explanation: Factory Records packaged 'Blue Monday' in a floppy disk sleeve that was so expensive to print they allegedly lost money on every copy.

questions.prompt: Cyndi Lauper became the first woman to have four top-five hits from a debut album in 1983 with which record?
questions.explanation: Hits included 'Girls Just Want to Have Fun', 'Time After Time', and 'She Bop'.

questions.prompt: Bon Jovi achieved global stadium rock status with which 1986 album featuring 'Livin' on a Prayer' and 'You Give Love a Bad Name'?
questions.explanation: Co-written with Desmond Child, 'Slippery When Wet' spent eight weeks at #1 on the Billboard 200.

questions.prompt: George Michael achieved massive solo critical and commercial success with which 1987 multi-platinum album?
questions.explanation: 'Faith' produced four Billboard Hot 100 #1 singles and won the 1989 Grammy Award for Album of the Year.

questions.prompt: Which 1987 Def Leppard album produced by Mutt Lange yielded six top 20 singles including 'Pour Some Sugar on Me'?
questions.explanation: 'Hysteria' was recorded after drummer Rick Allen lost his left arm in a car accident and learned to play a custom electronic drum kit.

questions.prompt: N.W.A released which controversial and influential 1988 gangsta rap album that launched Ice Cube and Dr. Dre?
questions.explanation: 'Straight Outta Compton' transformed West Coast hip-hop and sparked an official warning letter from the FBI.

questions.prompt: Tears for Fears scored worldwide #1 hits in 1985 with 'Shout' and which philosophical synth-pop single?

options.B: Everybody Wants to Rule the World

questions.explanation: 'Everybody Wants to Rule the World' won Best British Single at the 1986 Brit Awards.

questions.prompt: Which metal band released 'Master of Puppets' in 1986, widely considered the pinnacle of thrash metal?

nutrition-diet.title: Nutrition, Diet & Superfoods
nutrition-diet.description: Essential vitamins, minerals, macronutrients, gut health, superfoods and dietetics.

questions.prompt: Which fat-soluble vitamin is synthesized in human skin upon exposure to ultraviolet B (UVB) radiation?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol) is formed in the skin from 7-dehydrocholesterol when triggered by sunlight.

questions.prompt: A severe deficiency of which water-soluble vitamin causes scurvy, characterized by bleeding gums and poor wound healing?
questions.explanation: Ascorbic acid is an essential cofactor for prolyl and lysyl hydroxylase, enzymes vital for collagen synthesis.

questions.prompt: Which vitamin deficiency causes beriberi and Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome, common in chronic alcohol dependency?
questions.explanation: Thiamine is essential for carbohydrate metabolism and pyruvate dehydrogenase function in the nervous system.

questions.prompt: Pellagra, characterized by the 'four Ds' (diarrhea, dermatitis, dementia, and death), is caused by a deficiency in which nutrient?
questions.explanation: Niacin is required for NAD and NADP coenzymes; it can be synthesized from the amino acid tryptophan.

questions.prompt: Pregnant women are strongly advised to supplement with which B vitamin to prevent neural tube defects like spina bifida?
questions.explanation: Folate is critical for rapid cell division, DNA methylation, and closure of the embryonic neural tube in early pregnancy.

questions.prompt: Intrinsic factor, secreted by gastric parietal cells in the stomach, is required for the absorption of which essential vitamin?
questions.explanation: Vitamin B12 binds to intrinsic factor in the duodenum and is absorbed exclusively in the terminal ileum.

questions.prompt: Which fat-soluble vitamin is critical for the synthesis of blood clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X in the liver?
questions.explanation: Vitamin K acts as a cofactor for gamma-glutamyl carboxylase, enabling calcium binding on clotting proteins.

questions.prompt: Night blindness (nyctalopia) and xerophthalmia are early clinical signs of deficiency in which vitamin?
questions.explanation: Retinol combines with opsin in retinal rod cells to form rhodopsin, the visual pigment for dim-light vision.

questions.prompt: Which fat-soluble vitamin functions as a major lipid-soluble chain-breaking antioxidant protecting cell membranes from peroxidation?
questions.explanation: Alpha-tocopherol donates hydrogen atoms to lipid peroxyl radicals, preventing damage to polyunsaturated fatty acids.

questions.prompt: Rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults are classic signs of prolonged deficiency in which vitamin?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D regulates intestinal calcium and phosphate absorption necessary for normal bone mineralization.

questions.prompt: Which water-soluble vitamin is also known as riboflavin and imparts a bright neon yellow color to urine when taken in excess?
questions.explanation: Riboflavin is the precursor of flavin coenzymes FMN and FAD involved in cellular respiration.

questions.prompt: Which vitamin is commonly marketed for promoting healthy hair, skin, and nails, and is also known as Vitamin B7?
questions.explanation: Biotin serves as a coenzyme for five carboxylases essential in fatty acid, glucose, and amino acid metabolism.

questions.prompt: Which essential mineral is the central atom of the heme group in hemoglobin responsible for oxygen transport?
questions.explanation: Iron binds molecular oxygen reversibly in erythrocytes; iron deficiency causes microcytic hypochromic anemia.

questions.prompt: What type of dietary iron, found exclusively in animal flesh, has significantly higher bioavailability than non-heme plant iron?
questions.explanation: Heme iron is absorbed via heme transporter protein with 15-35% bioavailability compared to 2-20% for non-heme iron.

questions.prompt: Which mineral is required for the synthesis of thyroid hormones thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3)?
questions.explanation: Iodine deficiency causes compensatory enlargement of the thyroid gland, known clinically as goiter.

questions.prompt: Which intracellular cation plays the primary role in establishing resting membrane potential and counteracts sodium to lower blood pressure?
questions.explanation: High potassium intake facilitates urinary sodium excretion and relaxes vascular smooth muscle walls.

questions.prompt: Which trace element is a critical component of selenoproteins, such as glutathione peroxidase, which neutralize reactive oxygen species?
questions.explanation: Selenium protects against oxidative cell damage and supports normal thyroid hormone deiodination.

questions.prompt: Which mineral is the most abundant inorganic element in the human body, with 99% stored in teeth and bones?
questions.explanation: Calcium serves as both structural hydroxyapatite in bones and as a universal second messenger in cell signaling.

questions.prompt: Wilson's disease is an inherited metabolic disorder characterized by the toxic accumulation of which mineral in the liver and brain?
questions.explanation: Impaired biliary excretion of copper leads to Kayser-Fleischer rings in the cornea and neurological deficits.

questions.prompt: Hemochromatosis is a common genetic disorder leading to excessive intestinal absorption and tissue overload of which element?
questions.explanation: HFE gene mutations lead to iron deposition in the liver, pancreas ('bronze diabetes'), and myocardium.

questions.prompt: Which mineral serves as a cofactor for over 300 enzymatic reactions, including ATP stabilization, muscle relaxation, and protein synthesis?
questions.explanation: Magnesium ions stabilize ATP by coordinating with polyphosphate groups; deficiency can cause cardiac arrhythmias.

questions.prompt: Which trace mineral is essential for wound healing, immune T-cell function, DNA polymerase, and the senses of taste and smell?
questions.explanation: Zinc deficiency manifests as impaired wound healing, alopecia, hypogeusia (blunted taste), and immune dysfunction.

questions.prompt: Which mineral is added to public drinking water supplies in many countries to strengthen dental enamel against acid decay?
questions.explanation: Fluoride converts hydroxyapatite in tooth enamel into fluorapatite, which is far more resistant to acidic demineralization.

questions.prompt: How many kilocalories (kcal) of physiological energy are provided per gram of pure dietary fat?
questions.explanation: Fats are highly reduced hydrocarbons yielding approximately 9 kcal per gram, compared to 4 kcal/g for proteins and carbs.

questions.prompt: How many kilocalories of energy does one gram of pure ethyl alcohol yield?
questions.explanation: Alcohol provides 7 kcal/g, higher than carbohydrates and proteins, earning it the label of 'empty calories'.

questions.prompt: How many kilocalories per gram are yielded by dietary carbohydrates and proteins?
questions.explanation: Both digestible carbohydrates and proteins provide an average of 4 kcal (17 kJ) per gram.

questions.prompt: How many amino acids are considered 'essential' for adult humans because the body cannot synthesize them de novo?
questions.explanation: The 9 essential amino acids are histidine, isoleucine, leucine, lysine, methionine, phenylalanine, threonine, tryptophan, and valine.

questions.prompt: Which of the nine essential amino acids serves as the biochemical precursor to serotonin and melatonin?
questions.explanation: Tryptophan is converted into 5-HTP and then into serotonin in the central nervous system and gut enterochromaffin cells.

questions.prompt: Which amino acid is the direct precursor to catecholamines including dopamine, norepinephrine, and epinephrine?
questions.explanation: Tyrosine is converted to L-DOPA by tyrosine hydroxylase, the rate-limiting step in catecholamine synthesis.

questions.prompt: What polysaccharide serves as the primary storage form of glucose in human liver and skeletal muscle tissue?
questions.explanation: Glycogen consists of highly branched alpha-1,4 and alpha-1,6 glycosidic chains allowing rapid enzymatic mobilization.

questions.prompt: What digestive enzyme in human saliva begins the breakdown of dietary starch into maltose while chewing?
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase initiates starch digestion in the mouth until it is inactivated by gastric hydrochloric acid in the stomach.

questions.prompt: Which enzyme in the stomach requires an acidic pH (1.5-2.0) to cleave peptide bonds in dietary proteins?
questions.explanation: Pepsinogen is activated into active pepsin by stomach acid, breaking proteins into smaller peptide chains.

questions.prompt: Which green-yellow fluid produced by hepatocytes in the liver emulsifies dietary lipids in the small intestine?
questions.explanation: Bile salts contain amphipathic molecules that break large fat globules into microscopic micelles for lipase action.

questions.prompt: Which lipoprotein particle is popularly termed 'good cholesterol' because it transports cholesterol from tissues back to the liver?
questions.explanation: HDL facilitates reverse cholesterol transport, reducing atherosclerotic plaque accumulation in arteries.

questions.prompt: Which blood lipoprotein is known as 'bad cholesterol' because elevated levels cause atherogenic plaque formation in coronary vessels?
questions.explanation: Elevated circulating LDL particles penetrate vascular endothelial walls, undergo oxidation, and recruit macrophages into foam cells.

questions.prompt: Which dietary fats, created industrially via partial hydrogenation of vegetable oils, are banned in many nations due to cardiovascular risk?
questions.explanation: Industrial trans fats raise atherogenic LDL-C, lower protective HDL-C, and promote systemic vascular inflammation.

questions.prompt: Alpha-linolenic acid (ALA), eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) belong to which class of fatty acids?
questions.explanation: Omega-3 fatty acids possess their first double bond at the third carbon from the methyl end and reduce cardiovascular risk.

questions.prompt: Which plant oil has the highest concentration of monounsaturated oleic acid (18:1) and anchors the heart-healthy Mediterranean diet?
questions.explanation: Extra virgin olive oil contains over 70% oleic acid and phenolic antioxidants like oleocanthal and hydroxytyrosol.

questions.prompt: What is the primary physiological ketone body produced by the liver during prolonged fasting or ketogenic dieting?
questions.explanation: Beta-hydroxybutyrate serves as an efficient alternative fuel for the brain when glucose availability is low.

questions.prompt: What measurement ranks carbohydrate-containing foods based on how rapidly they raise blood glucose levels compared to pure glucose?
questions.explanation: High-GI foods (score >= 70) cause rapid spikes in blood glucose and insulin, whereas low-GI foods (<= 55) digest gradually.

questions.prompt: What term describes dietary non-digestible carbohydrates that selectively feed beneficial bacteria in the colon?
questions.explanation: Prebiotics such as inulin, fructooligosaccharides (FOS), and resistant starch stimulate Bifidobacteria and Lactobacilli.

questions.prompt: What term describes live microorganisms which, when administered in adequate amounts, confer a health benefit on the host?
questions.explanation: Common probiotic species include Lactobacillus rhamnosus, Bifidobacterium animalis, and Saccharomyces boulardii.

questions.prompt: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) like acetate, propionate, and butyrate are generated in the colon through the microbial fermentation of what?
questions.explanation: Butyrate is the primary energy source for human colonocytes and exerts anti-inflammatory, barrier-protective effects.

questions.prompt: Celiac disease is a genetically mediated autoimmune enteropathy triggered by the ingestion of which protein composite?
questions.explanation: Gluten proteins (gliadins and glutenins) found in wheat, barley, and rye cause villous atrophy in the small intestine.

questions.prompt: Lactose intolerance is caused by the physiological decline in intestinal brush border activity of which enzyme?
questions.explanation: Undigested lactose passes into the colon, drawing water osmotically and fermenting into hydrogen gas and cramps.

questions.prompt: The DASH diet was specifically formulated and proven by clinical trials to treat which cardiovascular condition?
questions.explanation: DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) emphasizes potassium, magnesium, calcium, and sodium restriction.

questions.prompt: Which traditional diet, rich in legumes, olive oil, whole grains, fish, and nuts, has the strongest evidence for cardiovascular longevity?
questions.explanation: Large prospective trials like PREDIMED demonstrated a 30% reduction in major cardiovascular events.

questions.prompt: Which seed, prized by the ancient Aztecs, absorbs up to 12 times its weight in water to form a mucilaginous soluble fiber gel?
questions.explanation: Chia seeds (Salvia hispanica) are rich in soluble fiber, alpha-linolenic acid, and plant protein.

questions.prompt: Which blue-green cyanobacteria biomass is commercially harvested as a rich protein and phycocyanin supplement?
questions.explanation: Spirulina is up to 60-70% protein by dry weight and contains potent antioxidant phycobiliproteins.

questions.prompt: Which ceremonial Japanese powdered green tea contains high concentrations of L-theanine and epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG)?
questions.explanation: Shade-grown matcha tea leaves are stone-ground entirely, delivering all catechins and amino acids directly.

questions.prompt: Which bright golden spice contains curcumin, a lipophilic polyphenol with documented anti-inflammatory properties?
questions.explanation: Curcumin bioavailability is enhanced up to 2,000% when consumed alongside piperine from black pepper.

questions.prompt: Which Andean pseudocereal is a rare complete plant protein containing all nine essential amino acids and is naturally gluten-free?
questions.explanation: Quinoa was revered as 'chisaya mama' (mother of all grains) by the Inca empire.

questions.prompt: Which purple berry native to the Amazonian palm tree Euterpe oleracea is celebrated for its antioxidant anthocyanin content?
questions.explanation: Açaí pulp has high concentrations of cyanidin 3-glucoside and healthy oleic and palmitic fatty acids.

questions.prompt: Which fermented Korean cabbage side dish is teeming with lactic acid probiotic bacteria like Leuconostoc and Lactobacillus?
questions.explanation: Kimchi fermentation yields lactic acid, vitamin C, carotenoids, and gut-protective bioactive peptides.

questions.prompt: Which fermented dairy beverage, originating in the Caucasus mountains, is cultured using symbiotic grains of yeasts and bacteria?
questions.explanation: Kefir contains up to 60 distinct strains of bacteria and yeasts, far more diverse than standard yogurt.

questions.prompt: What dark chocolate compound is a methylxanthine stimulant related to caffeine that provides mild vasodilation and mood elevation?
questions.explanation: Theobromine stimulates cardiac muscle and relaxes smooth muscle without the harsh jitters of caffeine.

questions.prompt: Which red wine polyphenol, found in grape skins, has been extensively studied for activating SIRT1 longevity pathways in animal models?
questions.explanation: Resveratrol is a stilbenoid produced by plants in response to pathogen injury or fungal stress.

questions.prompt: What is the primary symptom of severe Vitamin A toxicity (hypervitaminosis A)?

options.A: Intracranial pressure, hepatotoxicity, and peeling skin

questions.explanation: Excessive preformed retinol from supplements or polar bear liver causes dangerous intracranial pressure.

questions.prompt: Which compound in raw egg whites binds irreversibly to biotin, preventing its absorption unless cooked?
questions.explanation: Cooking denatures avidin, neutralizing its ability to sequester dietary biotin.

questions.prompt: What condition can arise in infants given unsupplemented cow's milk due to low iron and gastrointestinal micro-bleeding?
questions.explanation: Cow's milk contains little iron with low bioavailability and can cause microscopic intestinal blood loss in infants.

questions.prompt: Which B-vitamin is given in massive pharmacological doses to reduce high blood cholesterol but causes cutaneous flushing?
questions.explanation: Niacin-induced prostaglandin release causes intense skin warmth and flushing, often mitigated with aspirin.

questions.prompt: Which cooking method causes the greatest loss of water-soluble vitamins like Vitamin C and B-complex?
questions.explanation: Water-soluble vitamins leach out into the cooking water, which is often discarded.

questions.prompt: Which toxic chemical element mimics calcium in the body and is deposited into bones and teeth, causing chronic toxicity?
questions.explanation: Lead substitutes for calcium in biological enzymes, cross blood-brain barriers, and impairs neurodevelopment.

questions.prompt: Which heavy metal commonly bioaccumulates as toxic methylmercury in apex predatory marine fish like swordfish and shark?
questions.explanation: Methylmercury biomagnifies up the aquatic trophic web, prompting consumption limits for pregnant women.

questions.prompt: What is the clinical term for high blood potassium levels, which can trigger lethal cardiac arrhythmias?
questions.explanation: Hyperkalemia (> 5.0 mmol/L) disrupts cardiac conduction, causing peaked T-waves and ventricular fibrillation.

questions.prompt: Which dietary fiber fraction forms viscous gels in water and is effective at binding bile acids to lower LDL cholesterol?
questions.explanation: Oat beta-glucan and apple pectin form luminal gels that trap bile salts, forcing the liver to consume cholesterol to make more.

questions.prompt: Which cereal grain is the world's richest dietary source of cholesterol-lowering beta-glucan soluble fiber?
questions.explanation: The FDA approved a heart health claim for oat products containing at least 0.75g of soluble beta-glucan per serving.

questions.prompt: What is the primary biological function of brown adipose tissue (BAT) in human infants and cold-acclimated adults?
questions.explanation: Brown fat contains abundant mitochondria expressing Uncoupling Protein 1, dissipating proton gradients directly as heat.

questions.prompt: What endocrine hormone secreted by gastric endocrine cells stimulates hunger and appetite before a meal?
questions.explanation: Ghrelin levels rise during fasting to signal hunger to the arcuate nucleus in the hypothalamus.

questions.prompt: Which hormone secreted primarily by adipocytes (fat cells) signals satiety and long-term energy sufficiency to the brain?
questions.explanation: Leptin acts on hypothalamic receptors; obesity is commonly characterized by central leptin resistance.

questions.prompt: Which pancreatic hormone is secreted in response to rising blood glucose, facilitating glucose uptake into muscle and adipose cells?
questions.explanation: Insulin triggers translocation of GLUT4 glucose transporters to the plasma membrane.

questions.prompt: Which pancreatic alpha-cell hormone opposes insulin by stimulating hepatic glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis during fasting?
questions.explanation: Glucagon raises circulating blood sugar levels to maintain vital cerebral glucose supply.

questions.prompt: What metabolic pathway synthesizes glucose from non-carbohydrate precursors such as lactate, glycerol, and glucogenic amino acids?
questions.explanation: Gluconeogenesis occurs primarily in the liver and renal cortex during extended fasting.

questions.prompt: What is the resting metabolic rate (RMR) primarily determined by in healthy adults?

options.D: Lean fat-free body mass (muscle and vital organs)

questions.explanation: Metabolically active organs (liver, brain, heart, kidneys) and skeletal muscle account for ~70-80% of resting energy expenditure.

questions.prompt: What is the term for the increase in metabolic rate and energy expenditure associated with digesting, absorbing, and processing food?
questions.explanation: Protein has the highest TEF (20-30% of energy consumed), compared to carbs (5-10%) and fats (0-3%).

questions.prompt: Which essential fatty acid cannot be synthesized by humans and must be obtained from diet: Linoleic acid or Stearic acid?
questions.explanation: Linoleic acid (omega-6) and alpha-linolenic acid (omega-3) are the two strictly essential fatty acids for humans.

questions.prompt: Arachidonic acid (omega-6) is metabolized by cyclooxygenase (COX) enzymes into which pro-inflammatory signaling molecules?
questions.explanation: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) like ibuprofen work by inhibiting COX enzyme conversion of arachidonic acid.

questions.prompt: Which cooking oil has one of the highest smoke points (~270°C or 520°F), making it prized for high-heat searing?
questions.explanation: Refined avocado oil consists predominantly of stable monounsaturated fats with minimal free fatty acids.

questions.prompt: Which organ in the human body is the primary site of cholesterol synthesis?
questions.explanation: The liver synthesizes about 80% of endogenous cholesterol via the HMG-CoA reductase pathway.

questions.prompt: Statins reduce circulating cardiovascular cholesterol by inhibiting which rate-limiting enzyme in cholesterol biosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Inhibiting HMG-CoA reductase upregulates hepatic LDL receptors, clearing LDL particles from circulation.

questions.prompt: What condition results from acute water intoxication where excessive water intake dilutes serum sodium below 135 mmol/L?
questions.explanation: Severe hyponatremia causes cerebral edema, seizures, and can be fatal in endurance athletes who over-hydrate.

questions.prompt: Which organ excretes excess water-soluble vitamins when consumed beyond biological saturation?
questions.explanation: Water-soluble vitamins (B and C) are not stored in significant quantities and are readily cleared through renal glomerular filtration.

questions.prompt: Which organ stores a 2- to 5-year biological supply of Vitamin B12, preventing immediate deficiency on a plant-based diet?
questions.explanation: The human liver maintains large stores (2-5 mg) of cobalamin, meaning deficiency often takes several years to manifest.

questions.prompt: What antioxidant enzyme requires manganese as an essential catalytic cofactor in the mitochondrial matrix?
questions.explanation: MnSOD clears superoxide radicals produced by the electron transport chain inside mitochondria.

questions.prompt: Which component of cruciferous vegetables (like broccoli and kale) is hydrolyzed by myrosinase into anti-cancer sulforaphane?
questions.explanation: Chewing or chopping raw cruciferous vegetables activates myrosinase, releasing bioactive sulforaphane.

questions.prompt: Which bright red carotenoid antioxidant, found in high concentrations in cooked tomatoes, is linked to prostate health?
questions.explanation: Lycopene bioavailability increases when tomatoes are cooked in healthy fats like olive oil.

questions.prompt: Lutein and zeaxanthin are dietary xanthophyll carotenoids that selectively accumulate in which anatomical region of the human eye?

options.A: The macula lutea of the retina

questions.explanation: Lutein and zeaxanthin filter damaging blue light and neutralize photochemical free radicals in central macular vision.

questions.prompt: What dietary compound found in tea and coffee inhibits the intestinal absorption of non-heme iron when consumed with meals?
questions.explanation: Polyphenols and phytates bind non-heme iron to form insoluble complexes that cannot cross mucosal enterocytes.

questions.prompt: Ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) significantly increases the intestinal absorption of which dietary mineral?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C reduces ferric iron (Fe3+) to soluble ferrous iron (Fe2+) and prevents chelation by phytates.

questions.prompt: Phytic acid (phytate), abundant in raw grains and seeds, acts as an 'anti-nutrient' by chelating which essential minerals?
questions.explanation: Phytates bind divalent cations; traditional food preparation like soaking, sprouting, and sourdough fermentation degrades phytates.

questions.prompt: Which popular dietary supplement contains long-chain omega-3 fatty acids EPA and DHA extracted from tiny Antarctic crustaceans?
questions.explanation: Krill oil delivers EPA and DHA bound to phospholipids rather than triglycerides, enhancing cellular membrane incorporation.

questions.prompt: What compound gives hot chili peppers their pungent burning sensation by binding to TRPV1 heat receptors on tongue nerves?
questions.explanation: Capsaicin binds to thermal nociceptors, stimulating sensations of burning heat and triggering endorphin release.

questions.prompt: What organosulfur compound is rapidly produced when fresh garlic is crushed, yielding its pungent odor and antimicrobial properties?
questions.explanation: Crushing garlic breaks plant cell vacuole barriers, allowing alliin to react with the enzyme alliinase to form allicin.

questions.prompt: Which amino acid supplement is the precursor to nitric oxide, a powerful gaseous vasodilator that relaxes blood vessels?
questions.explanation: Nitric oxide synthase converts L-arginine into nitric oxide, promoting arterial endothelial blood flow.

questions.prompt: Which branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) is the primary trigger of the mTOR pathway, initiating muscle protein synthesis?
questions.explanation: Reaching the 'leucine threshold' (~2.5-3g per meal) maximally stimulates ribosomal translation and muscle repair.

questions.prompt: Creatine monohydrate supplementation enhances athletic performance by increasing cellular stores of what high-energy molecule?
questions.explanation: Phosphocreatine rapidly regenerates ATP from ADP during intense anaerobic sprint and power exertion.

questions.prompt: What is the primary protein found in milk whey, known for rapid digestion and rich branched-chain amino acid content?
questions.explanation: Whey comprises ~20% of cow's milk protein and digests rapidly, spiking circulating plasma leucine levels.

questions.prompt: What slow-digesting milk protein forms curds in the stomach, releasing amino acids steadily over several hours?
questions.explanation: Casein micelle structure precipitates in gastric acid, making it popular for sustained overnight muscle protein maintenance.

questions.prompt: Collagen supplements are rich in which three characteristic amino acids that form its triple-helix structural matrix?
questions.explanation: Glycine occurs at every third residue in collagen's polypeptide chains to permit tight triple-helix packing.

questions.prompt: Scurvy disrupts collagen synthesis specifically because Vitamin C is required to hydroxylate which two amino acids?
questions.explanation: Hydroxyproline residues are essential for stabilizing the collagen triple helix via interchain hydrogen bonds.

questions.prompt: What is the primary physiological storage organ for excess fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K)?
questions.explanation: Fat-soluble vitamins accumulate in hepatic stellate cells and body fat stores, making excessive supplementation risky.

questions.prompt: Hypercalcemia, calcification of soft tissues, and renal stones can be caused by massive chronic overdoses of which vitamin?
questions.explanation: Excess Vitamin D excessively increases gastrointestinal calcium absorption and bone resorption.

questions.prompt: Which water-soluble vitamin can cause peripheral neuropathy and nerve damage if taken in megadoses (> 200mg/day) for months?
questions.explanation: Excess pyridoxine can saturate neuronal metabolism and cause sensory ataxia and dorsal root ganglionopathy.

questions.prompt: Which artificial sweetener discovered in 1879 is 300-400 times sweeter than sucrose and has a metallic aftertaste?
questions.explanation: Saccharin was synthesized at Johns Hopkins University by Constantin Fahlberg and Ira Remsen.

questions.prompt: Which artificial sweetener consists of an ester of phenylalanine and aspartic acid and carries a warning for individuals with phenylketonuria (PKU)?
questions.explanation: Individuals with PKU lack phenylalanine hydroxylase and cannot metabolize phenylalanine safely.

questions.prompt: Which zero-calorie natural sweetener is extracted from the leaves of the South American plant Stevia rebaudiana?
questions.explanation: Steviol glycosides are up to 300 times sweeter than table sugar and do not elicit an insulin response.

questions.prompt: Which sugar alcohol (polyol) commonly used in sugar-free gum is toxic and potentially fatal to domestic dogs?
questions.explanation: Xylitol triggers a massive, rapid release of insulin in canines, leading to severe hypoglycemia and acute hepatic necrosis.

questions.prompt: Which sugar alcohol is absorbed in the small intestine but largely excreted unchanged in urine, minimizing gastrointestinal bloating?
questions.explanation: Erythritol is a 4-carbon polyol with low fermentability in the colon compared to 6-carbon sorbitol.

questions.prompt: What is the term for the biological clock-synchronized daily variation in glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity?
questions.explanation: Human insulin sensitivity is highest in the biological morning and declines towards late evening.

questions.prompt: What metabolic adaptation occurs during prolonged severe caloric restriction where the body burns fewer calories than predicted?
questions.explanation: The body downregulates leptin, thyroid T3, and sympathetic tone to conserve energy during famine.

questions.prompt: Which marine microalgae is the original primary producer of EPA and DHA omega-3s before small fish consume it?
questions.explanation: Vegan omega-3 supplements cultivate microalgae directly in closed bioreactors without ocean contaminants.

questions.prompt: Which vitamin is practically absent from unfortified, non-fermented plant foods, necessitating supplementation for strict vegans?
questions.explanation: B12 is produced exclusively by bacteria and archaea; plants neither produce nor require cobalamin.

questions.prompt: What compound found in rhubarb leaves and spinach forms insoluble crystals with calcium, causing sharp kidney stones?
questions.explanation: Calcium oxalate is the most common chemical constituent of human nephrolithiasis (kidney stones).

questions.prompt: Which metabolic process converts fatty acids into acetyl-CoA inside the mitochondrial matrix?
questions.explanation: Beta-oxidation sequentially cleaves two-carbon acetyl units from acyl-CoA chains to feed the citric acid cycle.

questions.prompt: What carrier molecule transports long-chain fatty acids across the inner mitochondrial membrane for beta-oxidation?
questions.explanation: Carnitine palmitoyltransferase-1 (CPT-1) attaches carnitine to fatty acyl groups to facilitate membrane translocation.

questions.prompt: Which coenzyme Q10 molecule is a lipophilic electron carrier in the mitochondrial inner membrane used for ATP generation?
questions.explanation: CoQ10 transfers electrons from complexes I and II to complex III in the electron transport chain.

questions.prompt: What is the principal intracellular antioxidant tripeptide composed of glutamate, cysteine, and glycine?
questions.explanation: Glutathione neutralizes reactive free radicals, protects red blood cells, and detoxifies hepatic drugs via conjugation.

questions.prompt: N-acetylcysteine (NAC) is administered in hospital emergency rooms as an antidote for toxic overdoses of which pain reliever?
questions.explanation: NAC replenishes hepatic glutathione stores to detoxify the reactive toxic metabolite NAPQI before it causes liver failure.

questions.prompt: What is the Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA) of Vitamin C for healthy adult men?
questions.explanation: The RDA for adult men is 90 mg/day, and 75 mg/day for adult women (plus 35 mg for smokers).

questions.prompt: What is the Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA) of Vitamin C for healthy adult women?
questions.explanation: Adult women require 75 mg/day to maintain tissue saturation and antioxidant defense.

questions.prompt: Smokers require how much additional Vitamin C per day compared to non-smokers due to oxidative stress?
questions.explanation: Cigarette smoke depletes circulating ascorbate, increasing metabolic turnover by 35 mg daily.

questions.prompt: What is the Tolerable Upper Intake Level (UL) for Vitamin C in healthy adults to avoid osmotic diarrhea?
questions.explanation: Intakes above 2g daily exceed intestinal absorption transporters, drawing water into the colon.

questions.prompt: What is the Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA) of calcium for adults aged 19-50?
questions.explanation: Adults require ~1,000 mg of calcium daily to preserve skeletal density and support neuromuscular signaling.

questions.prompt: What is the Tolerable Upper Intake Level (UL) for elemental calcium in young adults to prevent kidney stones?
questions.explanation: Excessive chronic calcium intake increases risks of hypercalcemia, vascular calcification, and nephrolithiasis.

questions.prompt: What is the World Health Organization (WHO) recommended maximum daily intake of sodium for adults?
questions.explanation: Limiting sodium below 2g (1 teaspoon of table salt) significantly reduces stroke and coronary heart disease risk.

questions.prompt: What is the adequate daily intake of dietary fiber recommended for adult men by the Institute of Medicine?
questions.explanation: Men under 50 are recommended to consume 38g of fiber, though average Western intake is only ~15g.

questions.prompt: What is the adequate daily intake of dietary fiber recommended for adult women by the Institute of Medicine?
questions.explanation: Women under 50 require 25g daily for gut health, glycemic control, and cardiovascular disease prevention.

questions.prompt: What is the primary dietary source of monounsaturated fatty acids in the avocado?
questions.explanation: Avocado pulp contains 60-70% monounsaturated oleic acid, identical to olive oil.

questions.prompt: Which medium-chain fatty acid constitutes approximately 50% of the total fatty acid content of coconut oil?
questions.explanation: Lauric acid is absorbed directly into portal circulation or packaged into chylomicrons.

questions.prompt: Which medium-chain triglyceride (MCT) with 8 carbons is most rapidly converted into ketones in the liver?
questions.explanation: Caprylic acid bypasses carnitine transport to rapidly undergo hepatic mitochondrial beta-oxidation.

questions.prompt: Which enzyme in human breast milk helps infants hydrolyze lipids before their pancreatic lipase matures?
questions.explanation: BSSL remains active in the neonatal intestine, ensuring efficient absorption of maternal fatty acids.

questions.prompt: What is the primary disaccharide found naturally in mammalian milk?
questions.explanation: Lactose is cleaved into glucose and galactose by the brush border enzyme lactase.

questions.prompt: Table sugar (granulated white sugar) is chemically classified as which disaccharide?
questions.explanation: Sucrose consists of one alpha-D-glucose molecule linked to one beta-D-fructose molecule.

questions.prompt: Which disaccharide is formed from two glucose molecules linked by an alpha-1,4-glycosidic bond?
questions.explanation: Maltose is produced during the enzymatic breakdown of starch by amylase in sprouted grains.

questions.prompt: Which plant polysaccharide cannot be digested by human enzymes and forms the primary insoluble fiber in plant cell walls?
questions.explanation: Cellulose consists of beta-1,4-linked glucose polymers that pass through the human GI tract intact.

questions.prompt: Which plant-derived soluble fiber extracted from citrus peels and apple pomace forms jams and jellies?
questions.explanation: Pectin forms cross-linked gel networks in acidic, high-sugar culinary preparations.

questions.prompt: What dietary seed husk is widely used as a bulk-forming soluble fiber laxative?
questions.explanation: Psyllium mucilage absorbs large amounts of water in the intestinal lumen, promoting stool regularity.

questions.prompt: Which essential mineral is a key component of the glucose tolerance factor (GTF) that potentiates insulin action?
questions.explanation: Chromium enhances the binding affinity of insulin to its cellular tyrosine kinase receptor.

questions.prompt: Which mineral deficiency is historically linked to Keshan disease, an endemic juvenile cardiomyopathy in China?
questions.explanation: Keshan disease occurs in regions with selenium-depleted volcanic soil and impairs myocardial antioxidant defense.

questions.prompt: Which mineral deficiency causes Kashin-Beck disease, a chronic deforming osteochondropathy?
questions.explanation: Low selenium and iodine in childhood disrupt chondrocyte survival in growing cartilage.

questions.prompt: What is the main biological function of the trace element Molybdenum in human metabolism?

options.C: Cofactor for sulfite oxidase and xanthine oxidase

questions.explanation: Molybdenum acts as the molybdenum cofactor (Moco), breaking down toxic sulfites and purines.

questions.prompt: Which mineral is an integral structural constituent of Cobalamin (Vitamin B12)?
questions.explanation: Cobalt sits coordinated at the center of the corrin ring system of Vitamin B12.

questions.prompt: What condition can develop from consuming massive quantities of raw cabbage, kale, and cassava due to thiocyanate goitrogens?
questions.explanation: Glucosinolate metabolites compete with iodine uptake in thyroid follicular cells via the NIS symporter.

questions.prompt: Which green leafy vegetable contains high concentrations of lutein, zeaxanthin, vitamin K, and folate?
questions.explanation: Raw and cooked spinach provides exceptionally dense micronutrient and carotenoid nutrition.

questions.prompt: Which cruciferous vegetable contains diindolylmethane (DIM), which modulates healthy estrogen metabolism?
questions.explanation: Indole-3-carbinol in cruciferous vegetables converts in stomach acid into DIM, promoting 2-hydroxyestrone.

questions.prompt: Which nutrient found in egg yolks and beef liver is an essential precursor for the neurotransmitter acetylcholine?
questions.explanation: Choline is also essential for synthesis of phosphatidylcholine in cell membranes and hepatic VLDL secretion.

questions.prompt: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) can be exacerbated by dietary deficiencies in which nutrient?
questions.explanation: Choline deficiency impairs phosphatidylcholine synthesis, preventing the export of triglycerides from hepatocytes.

questions.prompt: What is the main circulating form of Vitamin D measured in clinical blood tests to evaluate status?
questions.explanation: 25(OH)D has a 2- to 3-week circulating half-life, reflecting cumulative sunlight and dietary intake.

questions.prompt: Which organ performs the final 1-alpha-hydroxylation to activate Vitamin D into potent Calcitriol?
questions.explanation: Renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase is stimulated by parathyroid hormone (PTH) when blood calcium drops.

questions.prompt: Parathyroid hormone (PTH) is released by parathyroid glands in direct response to what physiological state?
questions.explanation: PTH restores serum calcium by stimulating renal reabsorption, intestinal absorption via calcitriol, and bone osteoclasts.

questions.prompt: Which hormone secreted by the thyroid gland's parafollicular C-cells acts to lower high blood calcium levels?
questions.explanation: Calcitonin inhibits osteoclast bone resorption, serving as a physiological antagonist to PTH.

questions.prompt: What is the primary protein found in human hair, fingernails, and the outermost epidermal skin layer?
questions.explanation: Keratin is an insoluble fibrous structural protein rich in cysteine disulfide crosslinks.

questions.prompt: Which amino acid provides the sulfur atoms responsible for the strong disulfide bridges that give hair its curl and strength?
questions.explanation: Disulfide bonds between cysteine residues determine hair curl; perms break and reset these covalent bonds.

questions.prompt: Which essential sulfur-containing amino acid is the obligate biological precursor to cysteine and taurine?
questions.explanation: Methionine is activated into S-adenosylmethionine (SAMe), the universal methyl donor in human biology.

questions.prompt: Elevated plasma levels of which toxic sulfur-containing intermediate are an independent risk factor for stroke and thrombosis?
questions.explanation: Hyperhomocysteinemia occurs when Vitamin B6, B12, or folate cofactors are deficient for remethylation or transsulfuration.

questions.prompt: Which B-vitamin is directly required to convert homocysteine back into methionine via methionine synthase?
questions.explanation: Methionine synthase requires methylcobalamin and 5-methyl-THF to transfer a methyl group to homocysteine.

questions.prompt: Which B-vitamin is required by cystathionine beta-synthase to convert homocysteine into cystathionine?
questions.explanation: Vitamin B6 drives the transsulfuration pathway, irreversibly routing homocysteine into beneficial glutathione synthesis.

questions.prompt: What is the primary dietary source of docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) for optimal infant brain and retinal development?

options.A: Fatty cold-water marine fish (and breast milk)

questions.explanation: DHA comprises over 30% of structural phospholipids in the cerebral cortex and photoreceptor disc membranes.

questions.prompt: Which enzyme in adipose tissue hydrolyzes stored triglycerides into free fatty acids during exercise and fasting?
questions.explanation: HSL is stimulated by epinephrine and glucagon, and strongly inhibited by circulating insulin.

questions.prompt: Which enzyme on capillary endothelial surfaces hydrolyzes circulating chylomicrons and VLDL to deliver fatty acids to tissues?
questions.explanation: Insulin activates LPL in adipose tissue, promoting the storage of dietary fat following a meal.

questions.prompt: What is the main physiological consequence of consuming high doses of fat-soluble Vitamin A during the first trimester of pregnancy?
questions.explanation: Excessive retinol disrupts cranial neural crest cell migration, causing severe congenital malformations.

questions.prompt: What non-toxic plant pigment is the primary precursor that the human body cleaves into active Vitamin A as needed?
questions.explanation: Beta-carotene 15,15'-dioxygenase cleaves beta-carotene symmetrically into two retinal molecules in enterocytes.

questions.prompt: Can consuming massive amounts of carrots or sweet potatoes cause dangerous Vitamin A toxicity?

options.B: Yes, it causes acute liver failure
options.D: No, it causes harmless orange skin discoloration (carotenodermia)

questions.explanation: The body downregulates the conversion of beta-carotene to retinol when vitamin A stores are replete.

questions.prompt: Which berry contains proanthocyanidins (PACs) that prevent uropathogenic E. coli bacteria from adhering to urinary tract walls?
questions.explanation: A-type proanthocyanidins in cranberries interfere with bacterial P-fimbriae binding to uroepithelial receptors.

questions.prompt: Which natural polyphenol found in red onions, capers, and apples acts as a mast cell stabilizer and antihistamine?
questions.explanation: Quercetin inhibits the release of histamine and inflammatory cytokines from sensitized basophils and mast cells.

questions.prompt: Which plant alkaloid found in barberry (Berberis vulgaris) activates AMPK and improves insulin sensitivity similarly to metformin?
questions.explanation: Clinical trials demonstrate berberine downregulates gluconeogenesis and upregulates glycolysis via AMPK activation.

questions.prompt: What is the primary antioxidant enzyme responsible for converting dangerous hydrogen peroxide into harmless water and oxygen?
questions.explanation: Catalase is located primarily in peroxisomes and possesses one of the highest turnover rates of all known enzymes.

questions.prompt: What toxic free radical is produced by the one-electron reduction of molecular oxygen during cellular respiration?
questions.explanation: Superoxide is rapidly converted to hydrogen peroxide by superoxide dismutase (SOD) enzymes.

questions.prompt: What is the most reactive and damaging free radical in human biology, formed via the Fenton reaction of iron with hydrogen peroxide?
questions.explanation: Hydroxyl radicals react instantaneously with lipids, proteins, and DNA at the diffusion-controlled limit.

questions.prompt: What heavy metal binds avidly to sulfhydryl groups in keratin, famously accumulating in hair and fingernails (Mees' lines)?
questions.explanation: Arsenic disrupts ATP synthesis by substituting for inorganic phosphate and causes characteristic transverse nail bands.

questions.prompt: Which toxic heavy metal found in cigarette smoke and industrial pigments accumulates selectively in renal proximal tubules?
questions.explanation: Cadmium binds to metallothionein, with a biological half-life of 10 to 30 years in the human kidney.

questions.prompt: What is the medical term for severe childhood protein malnutrition characterized by edema, moon face, and an enlarged fatty liver?
questions.explanation: Kwashiorkor occurs when caloric intake is marginally adequate (carbs) but protein is severely deficient.

questions.prompt: What is the medical term for severe generalized starvation and caloric deprivation characterized by wasting of all body fat and muscle?
questions.explanation: Marasmus manifests as a gaunt, elderly appearance without nutritional edema due to total calorie deficiency.

questions.prompt: What condition results from severe maternal iodine deficiency during fetal development, leading to profound cognitive and physical impairment?
